newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down, wait and see mood continues.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down, wait and see mood continues.

text.p: Czech shares continued to stagnate on Wednesday with foreign investors again staying on the sidelines and dealers seeing little hope of an upturn in the immediate future.
The PX50 dropped one point, 0.17 percent to 578.5 while the RPIX index recovered alightly after heavier early losses to close down 2.0 points, 0.16 percent, to 1,216.1.
"Maybe we predict a new recovery next month but not now," said Petr Opocensky of Citicorp Securities.
"Many investors and brokers are in wait and see mood," he added.

Opocensky echoed comments made by several other brokers in recent days that foreign investors were dissatisfied with the macroeconomic development of the Czech Republic where growth has been slowing sharply and real industrial output actually fell in January by 3.9 percent year-on-year.
The most significant decliner on the PX50 on Wednesday was SPT Telecom, by far the most heavily weighted share on the index accounting for 21 percent of its capitalisation.
SPT dropped 30 crowns to 3,590. Power utility CEZ recovered from heavy early loses to gain one crown to 1,089.
